Cut Paneer into squares. There should be 48 squares in total for 1 portion / 12 skewers. Marinate Paneer squares in Madras Spiced Marinade. Wearing gloves, gently use hands to mix well till fully incorporated.
Using a sharp knife, slice off the top green crown and about a half inch off the top of the Pineapple. Then slice off the base of the Pineapple to get a flat surface.
Remove the skin of the Pineapple by using a sharp knife to carefully cut away the skin / outer peel, from top to bottom, following the contours of the Pineapple.

Once skin is completely removed, remove the eyes of the Pineapple by making diagonal cuts across the side of the Pineapple, like a V-shaped trench. Remove all eyes of the Pineapple by cutting V-shape trenches while rotating the Pineapple.

Slice the Pineapple into half, lengthwise. Then lay down each pineapple half on the flat cut side, and cut it in half lengthwise again. Remove the core by cutting it out at an angle. Repeat with the remaining pineapples until the entire core has been removed. Discard core.
Then cut pineapples into 2 cm chunks. There should be 48 pineapple chunks in total for 1 portion / 12 skewers. Do not marinate the pineapple chunks in Madras Spice Marinade.

Skewer the Paneer and Pineapple by alternating between Paneer squares and Pineapple chunks. Each skewer should have a total of 4 Paneer squares and 4 Pineapple chunks. Repeat until all 12 skewers are completed.

Add mince to a mixing bowl. Add 2.5 tsp Himalayan Salt, 1 tsp Black Pepper Coarse, ½ tsp Ground White Pepper, 1 tbsp Dried Sage,½ tsp Ground Nutmeg, ½ tsp Cayenne Pepper, 1 tbsp Fresh Thyme, and Garlic Minced (2cloves) per 1kg of mince. Wearing gloves, use hands to mix well till fully incorporated.
Gradually add 80ml (5 tablespoons) of cold water while mixing to improve the sausage’s texture and help bind the ingredients.

Place all of the minced mixture into the sausage filler machine and attach Sausage Skin onto the machine. Tie the skin on the other end. Slowly fill the casing with mince while guiding it gently into a circular motion so it does not get damaged. Stop once the sausage becomes several metres long.

Working from the end of the filled casing, measure about 15-20 cm of sausage and twist the skin to mark a separation. Weigh this piece to ensure you get it between 165g. If you don’t, try the same process again till you get it. Once you do, cut it off and tie the loose end up in a knot. Use this piece as a
guideline to form all the rest of the sausages into this length and repeat the same process while arranging each sausage carefully in a tray.

Every layer of sausages in the tray needs to be layered with parchment paper to ensure they don't stick to each other. Once done, cling wrap the tray till air tight and place in a freezer for 24 hours.
Remove frozen sausages from the freezer. Wear gloves to lightly knock them apart so that they don't stick to each other.
Pack 1 sausages into medium vacuum seal bags and weigh each bag to ensure it is 160g - 170g. Vacuum seal using high pressure.
Attach “Cumberland Chicken Sausages” ear tags to the top of the packet using a stapler.
Tag expiry date to be 3 months from the date of production. Store in the freezer.

steps.instruction: Red bell peppers: , roasted 4 large (approx. 800 grams) and chopped Bird’s eye chili or any hot 10-15 (approx. 50-75 grams) chili): chopped Garlic: , minced 10 cloves (approx. 30 grams) Lemon juice: 120 ml (8 tablespoons) Olive oil: 240 ml (16 tablespoons) White vinegar: 120 ml (8 tablespoons) Paprika: 2 tablespoons (approx. 14 grams) Salt: 2 tablespoons (approx. 36 grams) Brown sugar: 2 tablespoons (approx. 28 grams) Oregano: 1 tablespoon (approx. 3 grams) Thyme: 1 tablespoon (approx. 3 grams) Bay leaves: 3 (approx. 2 grams) Black pepper: 1 tablespoon (approx. 6 grams) Cayenne pepper: 1 teaspoon (approx. 2 grams, optional for extra heat) Onion: 1 large (approx. 150 grams), chopped
Instructions:
Prepare the Ingredients:
Roast the red bell peppers until their skins are charred. Let them cool, then peel and chop them.
Chop the red chili peppers, onion, and mince the garlic.
Blend the Marinade:

In a blender or food processor, combine the roasted bell peppers, red chili peppers, garlic, lemon juice, olive oil, white vinegar, paprika, salt, brown sugar, oregano, thyme, black pepper, and cayenne pepper (if using).
Blend until smooth. Adjust salt and sugar to taste.
Cook the Marinade:
Pour the blended mixture into a large saucepan. Add the bay leaves.

Cool and Store:
Remove the bay leaves and let the marinade cool completely.
Transfer the marinade into sterilized jars or containers. Store in the refrigerator. Usage:
This marinade can be used for marinating chicken, beef, pork, or vegetables.
